images.title: The 0 holds the hundreds place
images.purpose: Shows 4072 as one digit per place, with 0 filling the empty hundreds place.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Four place boxes in a row with headers, one digit in each, the 0 box highlighted.
images.exact_structure: Four square boxes in a row with thin dark outlines, headed in grey (#6B7280): 1000s, 100s, 10s, 1s. Digits in the boxes in teal (#0072B2): 4, 0, 7, 2, except the 0, which is in green (#009E73) with a green box outline. Exactly 4 boxes and 4 digits. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In our numerals every place holds one digit, and 0 marks an empty place.
images.description: Shows 4072 as one digit per place, with 0 filling the empty hundreds place.

image_decisions.why: The job of 0 as a digit is clearest when the empty place is shown filled in a row of places.
